```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A has sourced evidence that the target buyer actually spends money. Cole County, MO paid $7,000 for a compliance tool in March 2026, and the Town of Templeton, MA was quoted $2,510 by CivicPlus/AudioEye. B's demand evidence is two Reddit posts, and neither shows anyone paying or willing to switch to a new paid vendor.",
    "A's pain is dated and externally imposed. Federal compliance deadlines fall on April 26, 2027 and April 26, 2028, sourced to ADA.gov and the Federal Register. Named municipal officials say they lack IT staff to comply. That is a forcing function. B's pain is complaints about price, and per B's own brief that pain is already solved by OneUptime's unlimited free public status page.",
    "A's sourced price anchors ($149/month for GovAccess, $0.30/page for CASO Comply) show a scanner-level product can sell at a modest price point. The briefs do not establish that such a sale avoids formal procurement.",
    "B's own brief says a new entrant is 'effectively selling against $0'. It also says the main acquisition wedge (SEO pages arguing the incumbent is overpriced) is already run by Hyperping. A solo entrant would have neither price nor channel advantage in 90 days.",
    "A has real risks: procurement friction, liability exposure, a crowded incumbent field, and possible further DOJ delays. Most of these sit in A's open questions rather than being confirmed as blockers. B's main blocker, free feature-complete competition, is documented with a source."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence. It consists of one Reddit comment about wanting a single incident URL and one Reddit thread title complaining that the market leader charges $399/month. Neither shows willingness to pay a new vendor. The price complaint is already answered by free and $9/mo alternatives listed in the same brief. The Instatus proof point (~$10k MRR) also cuts the other way: the brief cites only ~$500/mo MRR growth after years in market.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B's self-serve, low-price model could plausibly produce a first $9 to $29 sale faster than A's municipal sales cycle. A's 90-day risk is real but unquantified: the procurement timeline, insurance and reference requirements, and E&O coverage are all open questions with no evidence either way. I picked A because its evidence shows the buyer has budget and urgency. B's evidence shows the buyer has free alternatives. If A's procurement turns out to require RFPs or insurance certificates for even small purchases, this call would likely flip."
}
```
